resources.string: Point the phone at the ChArUco board: the overlay shows the pose and its error.
Calibrate the camera: Start, then move and tilt the board slowly through the frame until SAVED.
Calibrate the laser plane: Start, then sweep the stripe across the board at varied tilts.

Scan: Start, sweep the laser over the object; Export writes a Z-up PLY over the board (mm) to Download/EasyScanner and offers to share it. Photos takes posed full-resolution keyframes into an orbiter-native session (long press: one now); stopping it adds laser.ply.
Could not copy the scan to Downloads; it stays in the app\'s files.
This camera offers no photo size with the analysis aspect.
Lay the printed board flat and point the phone at it. The board\'s numbers are printed on the sheet.\nBoard: %1$s
✓ Board found: %1$d corners, %2$.1f px. If the grid lies on the print, it is the right board.
! %1$d markers seen but no board corners: the board in the settings is not the printed one.

Hold the phone where you will scan from — about as far from the board as from the object — and wait until the picture is sharp. Then lock the focus: a calibration only holds at the focus it was taken at.
The saved calibration was taken at %1$s.
Start, then move the phone slowly around the board: tilt it 30–45° to every side, near and far, so the board visits every part of the picture. It saves on its own.
Laser on, nothing on the board. Start, then sweep the stripe across the board, changing the phone\'s tilt between sweeps. It saves on its own.
The saved laser plane was fitted with an earlier camera calibration: calibrate it again.
Put the object on the board. Start, then sweep the laser over it and walk slowly around it, the board always in view.
Photos are taken on the way: hold still for a moment now and then.
Its points and photos are deleted from the phone.
Saved to %1$s/: %2$s (%3$d files). scan.ply is the cloud in mm, Z up; the folder as a whole is a session for orbiter-recon.\nOn a computer: connect the phone over USB and open Download/EasyScanner.
The scan session was closed and saved to %1$s.
The scan session was closed; copying it to Download failed, it stays in the app (%1$s) and is offered at the next start.
The copy to Download failed (%1$s). The scan stays in the app\'s files: %2$s
Nothing was captured: the scan had no points and no photos.
%1$d scan(s) were never copied to Download (latest %2$s, %3$d photos). Copy them now?
No scans yet. A guided scan or an expert-mode export lands here.
